Project Approach
Offeror shall submit a written Project Approach narrative
outlining its understanding of the scope of work, major
construction elements, anticipated constraints, sequencing
of critical activities, coordination with stakeholders, and
strategies for minimizing service disruptions. The approach
should demonstrate familiarity with the technical
challenges of the project, including work in State and Local
ROW, maintaining water service, and handling tie-ins, wet-
taps, and bypasses. The approach must also reference how
the Offeror plans to meet contract requirements and
incorporate applicable local, state, and agency standards.

Each Offeror can be awarded a maximum of 15 points
-0 pts – No project approach provided or completely generic
submission
-5 pts – Basic narrative submitted; lacks detail or site-specific
understanding
-10 pts – Clear understanding of scope; addresses major work -
activities and sequencing
-12 pts – Well-structured approach with discussion of technical
challenges, staging, and coordination
-15 pts – Comprehensive and detailed approach tailored to the
project, with specific methods for construction sequencing, risk
mitigation, stakeholder coordination, and quality control
sample:
Project Baseline Schedule
Offeror shall submit a baseline project schedule that
outlines all major construction phases, key milestones, and
proposed durations. The schedule must demonstrate logical
sequencing of work, compliance with the overall contract
time, inclusion of lead times for materials, and allowance
for coordination with other agencies (e.g., TXDOT, utility
owners). Offerors are encouraged to submit a bar chart or
Gantt-style schedule showing early completion
opportunities, critical path items, and realistic resource
allocation.

Each Offeror can be awarded a maximum of 15 points
-0 pts – No schedule submitted
-3 pts – Schedule submitted but lacks major milestones or
coordination details
-6 pts – Schedule aligns with contract duration and includes key
construction elements
-10 pts – Well-sequenced schedule including major tasks, long-lead
items, and agency coordination, and proper tie-ins within allowed
time windows.
-15 pts – Comprehensive schedule showing critical path, early
starts, float allowances, long-lead procurement, staging, and
realistic durations based on prior experience, testing, bypass
implementations, and proper tie-ins within allowed time windows.

Water Distribution Operator / Plumber
The project requires water line connections to existing
active water mains to be made under the direct supervision
of a Licensed Class C Water Distribution Operator (issued
by TCEQ) or a Master Licensed Plumber. The Offeror must
demonstrate that a qualified person meeting this
requirement is part of their team. Subcontractor experience
is allowed.

Each Offeror can be awarded either a pass or fail score
- Pass – Qualified individual identified (employee or
subcontractor)
- Fail – No qualified person identified
Offerors that fail to provide a qualified person may receive a
failing score and have their Offer rejected by Owner.
